title: Loop host space bound
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, let $I(x,s)$ be a predicate on Boolean words, and let $g(x,s)$ and $A(x,s)$ be Boolean-word-valued functions, with $A(x,s)$ Boolean-valued. Let $s_0$ assign a Boolean word to each Boolean word, and let $R,T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. Suppose that on every input $x$, $F$ halts within $T(|x|)$ steps with output the binary expansion of $R(|x|)$; that $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for every $x$; and that $I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,g(x,s))$. Suppose also that, for every $x$, the run of $B$ from its initial configuration on $x$ reaches the anchor state $a$ in some $t\le T(|x|)$, has not visited $a$ at any earlier time, and at time $t$ is exactly the anchor configuration with $s_0(x)$ on tape zero and all other work tapes blank. Finally, suppose that for every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$ there is a positive time $t\le T(|x|)$ such that the run of $B$ from that anchor configuration has no intermediate anchor visit; if $A(x,s)$ holds, it halts at time $t$ with output $g(x,s)$, and otherwise it is at the anchor configuration with $g(x,s)$ on tape zero and all other work tapes blank. Then, for every input $x$ and time $t$, the loop host with body $B$, fuel machine $F$, anchor $a$, and the specified mode uses at most $23K(T(|x|)+1)$ work-tape cells through time $t$, where $K$ is its number of work tapes.
